Converts each Records message on `records` into a Channels block of one `f64` sample per channel on `channels`, one channel per key in `channel_names`: latest-value control, such as a parameter an agent or a UI sets, read by a node that takes Channels. A key the record leaves out keeps its channel's latest value, 0 until a record names it; a key not in `channel_names` is ignored. A value is an integer or a float, or a boolean read as 1 or 0; a record that is not a map of string keys, or that holds another value under a name, is refused and writes nothing. Each block's start sample is the record's stamp since the first record's, counted at `sample_rate`, and always past the block before it.

outputs.documentation: One sample per record of each channel in `channel_names`

node_types.documentation: Converts one attribute of each Array frame on `array`, `attribute` (`samples` by default), into one Channels block on `channels`. The attribute is a CPU `[channels, samples]` tensor of `float32` or `float64`, one row per name in `channel_names`, and its samples are copied once into the block. The blocks are stamped at `sample_rate`, their start samples counted from the first block. A frame without the attribute, or whose attribute is GPU-resident, of another dtype or of another shape, is refused and writes nothing.

node_types.documentation: Converts one attribute of each Array frame on `array`, `attribute` (`image` by default), into one Image frame on `image` stating `format` (`rgba8_unorm` by default; also `rgba8_unorm_srgb`, `bgra8_unorm`, `bgra8_unorm_srgb`, `rgba16_float` and `rgba32_float`). The attribute is an `[h, w, 4]` tensor of the format's element type, its channels in the format's order: `uint8` for the 8-bit formats, `float16` for `rgba16_float` and `float32` for `rgba32_float`. A GPU attribute's pool slot becomes the Image frame's slot and nothing is copied, so the slot holds what `format` states, as an attribute `TextureToTensor` wrote does. A CPU attribute is copied once into a pixel buffer from this node's own output pool. A frame without the attribute, or whose attribute is of another dtype or another shape, is refused and writes nothing. Each Image frame states no colour.

inputs.name: array
inputs.documentation: The Array frames whose `attribute` is converted

inputs.name: attribute
inputs.documentation: The attribute of each Array frame read as the image.

inputs.name: format
inputs.documentation: The texture format each Image frame states, by its wire name.

outputs.name: image
outputs.documentation: One Image frame per Array frame

node_types.documentation: Converts each `rgba8_unorm` or `bgra8_unorm` Image frame on `image` into one `rgba8_unorm` Image frame on `rgba_image`, of the same size and colour, its channels in RGBA order. One GPU dispatch samples the frame into a texture, which one copy writes into a pixel buffer from this node's own output pool; a frame held in a pixel buffer is first copied into a texture. Each frame is written by the time it is sent. An sRGB frame would be decoded by the sampling, and any other format has no such kernel, so `image` takes neither, and one that arrives is refused and writes nothing.

inputs.name: image
inputs.documentation: The 8-bit RGBA or BGRA Image frames to convert

outputs.name: rgba_image
outputs.documentation: One rgba8_unorm Image frame per Image frame

node_types.documentation: Converts each Image frame on `image` into one Array frame on `array`, whose one GPU attribute `image` is the frame's own pool slot borrowed as an `[h, w, 4]` tensor: `uint8` for an `rgba8` or `bgra8` frame, `float16` for `rgba16_float` and `float32` for `rgba32_float`, its channels in the frame's own order. This node copies nothing. A reader whose device maps the slot linearly reads the tensor in place, at the slot's own address; one that cannot reads it through one GPU copy into a linear staging buffer, as a read of the Image frame itself does. The tensor's rows are the slot's rows, so a padded row pitch is a stride, never a copy. An `nv12` frame has two planes and no one-tensor layout, so `image` does not take one, and one that arrives is refused and writes nothing. A reader claims the slot when it reads the Array frame, so a producer that has recycled the slot by then makes the read a counted loss, never another frame's pixels.

inputs.name: image
inputs.documentation: The Image frames to borrow as tensors

outputs.name: array
outputs.documentation: One Array frame per Image frame, its slot as the `image` attribute
